method: Static reverse engineering; no specimen executed. Original samples inspected with atomscan and cleave facts; native x86 control/data flow with Rizin, CLR CIL with dnfile/dncil.

samples.marker: License webhook: explicit CLI value POST; theft claim corrected
samples.identification: 169-byte standalone Node.js CLI webhook sender; no package or installation provenance supplied.
execution: Entire source is unobfuscated: process.argv[2] -> licenseKey -> JSON.stringify({chaveAion: licenseKey}) -> fetch hardcoded HTTPS webhook with POST method. No filesystem, environment-secret access, credential-store lookup, code download, or response processing.
Top-level network operation is real and retained as notable; the word licenseKey does not prove an authentication credential or unauthorized disclosure.
samples.verdict_evidence: An explicit CLI input is the entire source of the transfer. A fixed webhook and license-named parameter alone do not establish stealing, spying, deception or a backdoor. BENIGN on the supplied standalone bytes; this is not an attestation to the endpoint operator.
samples.limits: Invocation, endpoint ownership, surrounding package and any wider compromise are unknown. Do not project behavior from an absent n8n dependency or hypothetical package.

samples.marker: Elex yyzUSB: wraps and overwrites host executables; traits retained
samples.identification: Native MSVC x86 yyzUSB resource-wrapper executable infector. PDBs name yyzUSB, Daemon and USBMonitorSrv. The collector filename does not establish Amadey, Remcos or SmokeLoader.
execution: 0x46b160 enumerates *.exe candidates and calls the wrapper through 0x44e4ba at 0x46b2ad.

0x46d550 obtains its own path, copies itself to tempfile (CopyFileW at 0x46d635, overwrite enabled), opens/reads the target, embeds those bytes as RCDATA type 10/name 99 (UpdateResourceW at 0x46d731), commits, then overwrites the target with the resulting wrapper (0x46d7b3) and removes the temporary file.

0x46d970 copies the carrier, loads its resources, writes the retained host executable and starts it with CreateProcessW. RCDATA 99 contains a Microsoft VSTOInstaller host. Other executable resources carry matching yzzusb2 build paths.
0x47eb20 and 0x47f760 inventory logical drives; download setup at 0x464f30 dynamically resolves URLDownloadToFileW. Configured download URLs use example.com, so no operational C2 is asserted.

0x471270 passes PhysicalMemory to dynamically resolved native calls and edits its security ACL. 0x471bc0 loads ntoskrnl.exe and resolves KeServiceDescriptorTable and related exports. ZhuDongFangYu.exe security-product targeting corroborates the anti-AV profile. OpenFileMappingA at 0x47cdee supplies separate mapped-memory access context; the existing description correctly states references rather than claiming a proven SSDT write.
samples.verdict_evidence: The executable-selection loop and linked self-copy/resource wrapping/overwrite sequence establish unauthorized host infection, independent of the family name, sandbox score, or download success.
samples.limits: No execution, deployment authorization or operator provenance available. Three embedded PE analysis units remain present. Atomscan carves broad embedded spans; exact resource extraction additionally identified the original VSTO host and two support executables. No new allegation against the legitimate host is made.

samples.marker: Alhena implant: keylogging and ransom attempts; service rule added
samples.identification: Small unsigned .NET surveillance/backdoor and ransomware-attempt executable, masquerading as Microsoft Windows Update Service. NanoCore labels and placeholder files do not establish that it is authentic NanoCore.
execution: Main (RVA 0x2908) checks native and managed debuggers, VM/timing gates, copies itself, writes Startup and Run-key persistence, schedules an onlogon task, attempts ms-settings/DelegateExecute fodhelper elevation, disables Defender and creates an administrator account.

Main starts KeyloggerModule (low-level hook). HookCallback reads the key value and appends window/timestamp records; SendLoop writes keylog.txt and calls SendToC2. Separate callbacks capture clipboard contents, JPEG screenshots and selected user files; password-recovery code sends Chromium stores and stages Windows Credentials files.

StartReverseShell callback (RVA 0x3b88) creates TcpClient and cmd.exe with redirected streams. Closure methods at RVAs 0x3b10 and 0x3b4c relay command output to the socket and socket input to cmd stdin. HTTP tasking dispatches received commands, browse/file requests, registry operations and host control commands.

SendToC2 (RVA 0x42b4) UTF-8 encodes, XORs with key[i]=i^0xaa, Base64 encodes and URI-escapes records into a WebRequest GET. Config sets C2_DOMAIN to http://alhena.io while the sender prepends http:// again; the TCP client also receives the scheme-prefixed string. Successful communication is not established.

RealEncryption callback (RVA 0x4718) recursively targets Desktop/TestFolder, reads files, initializes AES/CryptoStream, intends to write .encrypted siblings and delete originals. AES key is 16 bytes; configured IV H1ddenT3ars1v!! is 14 bytes, causing IV assignment failure before file replacement. Ransom notes/payment demands and wallpaper are still attempted; no successful encryption claim.

Main invokes shadow-copy deletion, SafeBoot deletion, System Restore disabling, IFEO debugger hijacking and tool killing. DisableWindowsSecurityCenter (RVA 0x5604) sets wscsvc Start=4 and invokes Process.Start("sc", "stop wscsvc"). New rules cover this previously missed stop-command behavior.

ProcessHollowing is actually a remote allocation/write/thread sequence, already detected as neutral remote-thread APIs; the label alone is not treated as image hollowing. Webcam code uses 0x425 rather than the 0x419 SaveDIB message; microphone PowerShell attempts invalid AxHost-based recording. Neither is promoted to confirmed recording from module names.
samples.verdict_evidence: Covert key recording, remote cmd bridging, credential/file collection, malicious persistence and security sabotage establish hostile intent despite broken configuration and ransom code. There is no evidence of an authorized remote-administration deployment.
samples.limits: Effects depend on permissions, configuration and runtime reachability. Several methods are flawed or placeholders. Existing traits generally describe references/profiles or attempts; all supported detections remain.

rule_corrections: Relocate the exact Easypanel endpoint matcher from exfiltration to neutral HTTP/webhook at notable. An endpoint reference is not evidence of concealment; retain its matcher and unix/windows/fortios scope. Remove test suppressions because the address is still accurately observable there.
Relocate the unchanged license-body syntax matcher into metadata/lang/source/syntax/key-value. The regex supports syntax, not theft or a bound request.

Replace webhook-license-credential-exfil with the same required observations under micro-behaviors/communications/http/webhook::licensekey-body-at-fixed-webhook, notable. It describes co-occurrence, not unauthorized transfer.

Update both exact consumers: system-profile exfil keeps its hostile finding; the randomized n8n clone consumer now describes a fixed license webhook at suspicious, since its required legs do not establish credential stealing. The separate general clone observation is retained.
Add notable Security Center stop-command arguments and a hostile keylogger/launch/stop-argument composite. Descriptions state references, not bound execution or successful termination.

consumer_and_fixture_audit.searched: Exact IDs plus exfiltration/messaging ancestors, new HTTP/webhook and key-value ancestors; existing regression records and positive fixture scripts inspected before correction.
tests: 19 focused files and archive members passed baseline/current comparison, including real standalone sample source, independent existing hostile webhook/file-exfil fixtures, benign notification/license controls, the exact n8n archive consumer, retained system-profile exfil and service-stop positive/near misses.
All Elex findings across the parent and three embedded PE analyses retained. All Alhena findings retained; two added.

detection_losses_and_disagreements: Only unsupported theft/endpoint-suspicion claims were removed or reduced; their underlying observations remain. The n8n license clone consumer loses an unsupported hostile theft claim, retaining a suspicious clone/webhook observation. No supported attack finding was lost in the samples or focused positives. Current calibrated ML verdicts agree with the review; the standalone webhook was already calibrated BENIGN before correction despite the 0.990 raw score and hostile YAML finding. Native scores remain 0.99 and 0.98.
external_context: Supplied tria.ge URLs were attempted but unavailable through the web tool. Verdicts use local bytes and control flow; unrelated search results were not used as evidence.
